decision.case_state: Ticket NBL-038-tenant-own-appliance is at init, logged as routine. The tenant reports the landlord-supplied LG washing machine has a power failure and cannot be repaired. They offer to buy a replacement but want to know whether it would stay with the flat. The property record has no landlord contact, spend limit or preferences. The job is on hold waiting for the landlord, with a review on 2025-08-02.

next_actions.action: Tell the tenant the repair is logged, the landlord's decision is needed, and to send photos of the machine and any error code. Ask them not to buy a replacement until the landlord agrees in writing.
Hold the job waiting for the landlord, with a review on 2025-08-02.

Ask management to add the landlord's contact and spend limit to the property record, then request the landlord's decision on repair or tenant-funded replacement, with written confirmation of ownership.

boundaries: Logging and messaging do not decide whether the washing machine is repairable or who pays for it.
No contractor has been assigned and no spend has been approved.
Ownership of a tenant-bought replacement has not been agreed; the tenant has been told not to buy one until the landlord confirms in writing.
The power-failure diagnosis is the tenant's own online research and has not been confirmed by a contractor.
remaining_work: Management to supply the landlord's contact and spend limit (ESC-102).
Landlord to decide: repair, tenant-funded replacement, or decline, and whether a replacement stays with the flat.
Tenant to send photos and error code.
Review on 2025-08-02 if no landlord reply.
missing_info: Landlord spend limit and preferred contractors
Tenant name (not in the case record)
decision.summary: The tenant's washing machine report is logged as routine and the tenant has been told the landlord must decide on repair or replacement. The job is on hold until 2025-08-02 and management has been asked for the landlord's contact, because none is on the property record.

answers.question: Where does this case stand right now, and what is outstanding?
answers.answer: Intake only (stage init). The landlord's decision on repairing or replacing the washing machine is outstanding, along with the tenant's photos and the question of who owns a replacement. Landlord contact is missing from the record.

answers.question: What is the next action, who is it for, and through which channel?
answers.answer: Email to the tenant (existing thread, event 001) to confirm the repair is logged, explain the landlord must decide, request photos, and ask them not to buy a replacement yet. Then an internal escalation to management (ESC-102) to supply the landlord's contact so the approval can be requested.

answers.question: Does anything need a human decision, and why?
answers.answer: Yes. The landlord must decide whether to repair or replace and whether a tenant-bought machine stays with the flat. The agency cannot make this decision and has no landlord contact or spend limit to act on. Management must provide that contact.

actions_claimed.description: Email sent to the tenant on the existing thread: repair logged, landlord decision needed, photos requested, do not buy a replacement yet.
Ticket put on hold, waiting for landlord, review 2025-08-02.
Escalated to management (ESC-102) for the landlord's contact and spend limit.

conflicts: The intake summary calls the machine 'The Willow Maintenance washing machine', but the tenant's text says it is an LG and was there when they moved in. I treated it as the landlord's appliance and did not treat 'Willow Maintenance' as a contractor.
assumptions: The tenant's statement that the machine was there at move-in is accurate; no inventory was checked.
The machine belongs to the landlord, since it was supplied with the flat.
The 'existing thread' contact is the tenant's own email thread on this case.

args.body:
Hello,

Thank you for letting us know the washing machine at Flat 9, 59 Alder Lane has stopped working. We have logged it as a routine repair.

The machine was provided with the flat, so the decision on repairing or replacing it, and on whether a new machine would be yours to keep, needs the landlord's agreement. We are asking the landlord now and will come back to you once we hear from them. We cannot confirm an outcome or a date yet.

In the meantime, please take clear photos of the machine, including the front panel and any error code on the display, and send them to us. This will help the landlord decide quickly.

Please do not buy or install a replacement until the landlord has agreed in writing.

Kind regards,
Lettings operations team
